thread:
amy: Quick update — NebulaPay is asking for a POC stress summary and a pricing delta for sustained traffic. They want: 1) 500 concurrent request profile w/ 256 tokens inc. response 2) p50/p95 tail lat + ops notes 3) hosted vs dedicated cost to hit ~10M tokens/day. Can someone paste the last run results? :pray:
jordan: I ran the 500-concurrency run yesterday against redwood-13B-quant (fp16 -> int8 path). K6 script attached in the thread. Raw numbers below.
samir: TL;DR: p50=65ms, p95=420ms, p99~780ms for generate tokens part only (seq=256, batching=8, KV caching on warm cache). Sustained throughput ~3.8k tok/s across the pool. CPU on host proxies ~45%, GPU util ~62% avg. GPU mem headroom ~4GB.
lina: Helpful. Do we have the exact k6/locust command and the model server config so ops can reproduce in their environment? Also NebulaPay wants TLS+mutual auth and VPC peering — any blockers?
jordan: k6 command I used:
```
k6 run --vus 500 --duration 10m ./scripts/stream-gen.js --summary-export=nebula-run.json
```
stream-gen.js uses 1 request per VU with chunked streaming parsing. Model server cfg (production-ish):
```
{ "model": "redwood-13B-quant", "max_seq": 256, "batch_size": 8, "prefill": true, "kv_cache": true }
```
Replay note: warm cache for ~2m before measurements.
samir: Repro tips: 1) warm KV cache by running low-concurrency warmers, 2) set client side socket timeouts to 30s, 3) disable autoscale step-down during run (keeps backend steady).

Cost math (rough):
- Hosted (payg): based on last month billing, redwood-13B-quant ~ $0.00055 per input+output token equivalent (token accounting depends), so 10M tokens/day ~ $5.5k/day => ~$165k/mo.
- Dedicated: 1 dedicated pool (8x A10G equiv) + infra ~ ~$35k/mo committed. With that pool we can hit ~12M tokens/day at similar latency depending on burst profile. Break-even ~3-4 weeks depending on utilization.

jordan: Security: VPC peering + mTLS + enterprise audit logging are supported on Private/Dedicated. For hosted, we can offer customer-managed KMS and audit exports but cannot do VPC peering unless they opt for Private deployment.

amy: NebulaPay also asked about SLA for p95 under 500 concurrent. Can we commit? risky to promise 95th at 500 without dedicated capacity.
samir: Agree — on Hosted we quote best-effort; on Dedicated we can guarantee latency SLOs per contract. If they need contractual p95@500 we'd push Dedicated with canary and run a 72h soak.
lina: I'll flag the security questionnaire: question about data residency and deletion. Answer: data-in-transit encrypted, hosted logs retained per contract, Private gives full data residency. I'll drop a draft answer later.
jeff (deploy-bot): Dedicated pool scaling event: pool-redwood-42 scaled from 6->8 nodes at 2026-03-03T18:22:12Z for capacity testing. :robot_face:

amy: Next steps: 1) Lina to provide draft security QA 2) Samir to export reproducible k6 script + docker-compose for model server 3) Jordan to prepare 30/60/90 day cost scenarios for hosted vs dedicated 4) Run a 72h dedicated soak if they sign NDA. Can we get those by EOD tomorrow?
jordan: I'll post the cost sheet and run link in a follow-up. attaching nebula-run.json (summary) — I'll DM the raw logs to sales.
samir: I'll drop the k6 script + docker-compose into the shared drive and link here tomorrow AM.
lina: Draft security QA will be in the doc by EOD. tagging @amy @jordan for awareness. :thumbsup:
amy: Thanks team — shipping this to NebulaPay now. :rocket:
